$comment: One entry per shipped natural page clip, written by tools/render-pages.py. Exact displayed text and hashes make stale or replaced narration detectable. Quick Words are never part of this text.

city-water-moves/canals.text: Canals are wide water roads in the city. They carry the water toward the river.

city-water-moves/closing.text: Across the city, water keeps moving.

city-water-moves/deep-tunnels.text: Deep under the city, big drainage tunnels carry water fast to the river.

city-water-moves/drains-and-pipes.text: Under the streets, drains and pipes catch the water and lead it away.

city-water-moves/floodgates.text: Floodgates open to let water out. Floodgates close when the river is higher than the canal.

city-water-moves/hard-surfaces.text: A city is full of hard surfaces. Roofs and roads cannot drink rain, so the water must be carried.

city-water-moves/monkey-cheek.text: Parks and ponds can hold water like a monkey holds food in its cheeks. In Thailand, this is called the Monkey Cheek scheme.

city-water-moves/one-team.text: Drains, canals, gates, pumps, tunnels and ponds work as one drainage system. They give the water a way out, or a place to wait.

city-water-moves/pumps.text: When gates close, pumps push the canal's water up into the river.

comets/coma-grows.text: Near the Sun, some ice turns into gas. A fuzzy cloud called a coma grows around the comet.

comets/comet-dust.text: Comets leave trails of dust. When Earth crosses a trail, we see a meteor shower of shooting stars.

comets/dirty-snowball.text: A comet is a ball of ice, dust and rock. People sometimes call it a dirty snowball.

comets/far-and-faint.text: Most of the time, comets are far from the Sun. They are too faint for us to see.

comets/goodnight-comet.text: The comet follows its long path into the dark. Goodnight, comet. We will watch for you again.

comets/halley-returns.text: Some comets come back again and again. Halley's Comet returns about every 76 years and will come back around 2061.

comets/long-path.text: A comet travels around the Sun on a long, stretched path.

comets/two-tails.text: The comet grows two tails: a curved dust tail and a straighter gas tail. Both point away from the Sun.

discovery:street-under-water/look-under-.text: Objects can hide under the water.
The water can hide a deep drain.
Stay away from electrical things near floodwater.
The road may not be flat underneath.
Floodwater can carry germs and dirty things.

gems/amethyst.text: Amethyst is purple quartz. Quartz comes in many colors.

gems/back-home.text: Our gems sparkle in the sun. Which one is your favourite?

gems/crystals.text: Many gems are crystals. The tiny parts inside a crystal line up in a neat pattern.

gems/cutting.text: A gem cutter shapes and polishes a rough stone. The flat faces, called facets, catch the light.

gems/diamond.text: A diamond is made of carbon. It is the hardest natural material.

gems/geode.text: A geode looks like a plain rock. Inside, it is lined with sparkling crystals.

gems/minerals.text: Most gems are minerals. Minerals are made by nature, and they are not alive.

gems/opal.text: Opal flashes with rainbow colors. Tiny shapes inside it bend the light.

gems/pearl-amber.text: Some gems come from living things. Pearls grow inside oysters, and amber is tree sap that turned hard.

gems/ruby-sapphire.text: Rubies and sapphires are the same mineral. Tiny bits of other elements give them different colors.

gems/underground.text: Many gems grow slowly underground. Heat and pressure help them form.

gems/what-is-a-gem.text: A gem is a beautiful stone. People have loved gems for a very long time.

how-dams-work/closing.text: A storage dam holds water for later and releases it when people and rivers need it.

how-dams-work/making-room.text: Using the forecast, the people who run the dam can decide on a pre-release. Letting some water go early makes room in the lake for the new rain.

how-dams-work/not-all-dams.text: Big dams like Bhumibol and Sirikit are storage dams. They store water for later use. The Chao Phraya Dam is a diversion dam. Its gates share the river's water between canals.

how-dams-work/spillway.text: A spillway is a safety path for extra water. It carries big flows safely past the dam.

how-dams-work/store-and-release.text: Water flowing into the reservoir is inflow. The dam releases water for farms, homes and power.

how-dams-work/two-numbers.text: How much water is stored is one number. How much water passes each second is another. Stored water is measured in millions of cubic metres. Flow is measured in cubic metres each second.

how-dams-work/upstream-downstream.text: The river above the dam is upstream. The river below is downstream. Good dam choices care for both.

how-dams-work/wall-and-lake.text: A dam is a strong wall. The lake behind it is the reservoir.

how-dams-work/where-water-comes-from.text: Rain falls across the catchment — all the land that sends water to the reservoir. Streams carry it in. This arriving water is called inflow.

how-much-rain/accumulated.text: The rain adds up. The total is accumulated rainfall. First five, then ten more, then fifteen more.

how-much-rain/closing.text: Next time it rains, we can read our own rain gauge.

how-much-rain/measuring-network.text: Weather stations across Thailand measure the rain.

how-much-rain/news-numbers.text: When the news says one hundred millimetres, picture one hundred litres on every square metre.

how-much-rain/one-millimetre.text: One millimetre of rain is one litre of water on every square metre.

how-much-rain/rain-gauge.text: A rain gauge catches the rain. Its scale tells us how many millimetres of rain fell.

how-much-rain/rain-intensity.text: Rain can fall fast or slow. Fast rain is called heavy rain. Slow rain is light rain.

how-much-rain/short-vs-long.text: A short heavy shower and a long gentle rain can give the same total.

how-much-rain/ten-millimetres.text: Ten millimetres of rain gives ten litres on every square metre.

jupiter-great-red-spot/a-fast-spin.text: Jupiter spins very fast. One day there lasts only about ten hours.

jupiter-great-red-spot/a-gas-giant.text: Jupiter is a gas giant. It has no solid ground where we could stand.

jupiter-great-red-spot/colourful-cloud-b.text: Cream, orange and brown clouds wrap around Jupiter in bands. Strong winds push neighbouring bands in different directions.

jupiter-great-red-spot/cover.text: Jupiter and the Great Red Spot

jupiter-great-red-spot/faint-rings.text: Jupiter even has rings. They are thin, dark and hard to see.

jupiter-great-red-spot/fire-and-ice.text: Io has many active volcanoes. Europa has an icy shell with a deep ocean below it.
jupiter-great-red-spot/fire-and-ice.sent_text: Eye-oh has many active volcanoes. Europa has an icy shell with a deep ocean below it.

jupiter-great-red-spot/four-big-moons.text: Many moons travel around Jupiter. The four biggest are Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto.
jupiter-great-red-spot/four-big-moons.sent_text: Many moons travel around Jupiter. The four biggest are Eye-oh, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto.

jupiter-great-red-spot/goodnight-jupiter.text: The children imagine flying past the giant planet and its moons. Goodnight, Jupiter. Goodnight, Great Red Spot.

jupiter-great-red-spot/the-biggest-plane.text: Jupiter is the biggest planet in our Solar System. It is so wide that eleven Earths could fit across it.

jupiter-great-red-spot/the-great-red-spo.text: The Great Red Spot is a giant storm bigger than Earth. It has lasted for hundreds of years, but it has been shrinking.

mars-landforms/a-land-of-giant-volcanoes.text: Mars has a great volcanic region called Tharsis. Huge volcanoes rise above its plains. One of them is bigger than all the others.

mars-landforms/a-mountain-hundreds-of-ki.text: Olympus Mons is not a narrow, pointy mountain. It is a giant shield volcano with wide, gentle slopes. Its base is more than 600 kilometres across.

mars-landforms/a-world-that-changed.text: Mars has changed over billions of years. Water flowed. Volcanoes grew. Canyons and craters recorded its history. Today Mars is cold and dry, but its old landscapes still tell us what happened long ago.

mars-landforms/at-the-top-of-olympus-mon.text: At the top are huge pits called calderas. Magma once moved away from below the summit. Then parts of the ground collapsed and sank.

mars-landforms/built-by-lava.text: Long ago, lava flowed across Olympus Mons again and again. The lava spread far over the ground. Layer by layer, the volcano grew wider and higher.

mars-landforms/cover.text: Mars: Giant Volcanoes and a Great Canyon

mars-landforms/down-into-valles-marineri.text: Some parts of Valles Marineris are hundreds of kilometres wide. The deepest places reach about nine kilometres down. Its cliffs expose layer after layer of Martian rock.

mars-landforms/meet-olympus-mons.text: This is Olympus Mons. It is the largest known volcano in the Solar System. It is so huge that we need to look from far above to see its shape.

mars-landforms/the-great-canyon.text: Mars has another giant landform. This is Valles Marineris, a vast system of canyons. It cuts across thousands of kilometres of Mars.

mars/a-blue-sunset.text: Mars is the Red Planet. But near sunset, something surprising can happen. The sky around the Sun can glow blue.

mars/a-cold-world.text: Mars is usually very cold. Even when the Sun shines, the ground can be freezing. Mars is a cold desert.

mars/a-day-called-a-sol.text: Mars turns around and around. One day on Mars is called a sol. A sol is only a little longer than a day on Earth.

mars/a-long-martian-year.text: Mars has seasons too. It has spring, summer, autumn and winter. But one year on Mars lasts 687 Earth days.

mars/a-world-of-many-shapes.text: Mars is not flat and empty. It has plains, craters, mountains, volcanoes and deep valleys. Every place has a story.

mars/ice-on-mars.text: Mars has ice. There is water ice at its poles and under parts of the ground. In winter, even carbon dioxide can freeze into ice.

mars/mars-long-ago.text: Mars did not always look the way it does today. Billions of years ago, liquid water flowed across its surface. Mars was wetter than it is now.

mars/meet-mars.text: This is Mars. Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. It is a cold, rocky world.

mars/rivers-lakes-and-deltas.text: Rivers once cut valleys into Mars. Water filled some craters and made lakes. Where rivers met lakes, they sometimes built deltas from mud and sand.

mars/the-thin-air.text: Mars has an atmosphere. But its air is very thin. It is made mostly of a gas called carbon dioxide.

mars/why-is-mars-red.text: Mars is called the Red Planet. There is iron in its rocks and dust. The iron has changed into rusty minerals, making Mars look red.

mars/wind-and-dust.text: The Martian air is thin, but it can still move. Wind lifts the fine red dust. Sometimes huge dust storms spread across Mars.

reading-flood-news/accumulated-decoded.text: Accumulated rainfall is rain added up over a set time, like one whole day.

reading-flood-news/closing.text: Now the news makes sense. Next time we hear it, we can explain it.

reading-flood-news/closures-decoded.text: A closed road keeps cars away from deep water. This is a road closure. Barriers are helpers.

reading-flood-news/flash-flood-decoded.text: A flash flood arrives quickly, in hills or in towns. Families move to the marked safe high ground and wait.

reading-flood-news/level-decoded.text: The water level tells how high the river surface is on its gauge. Rising or falling matters most.

reading-flood-news/low-lying-decoded.text: A low-lying area is low, flat ground. Water collects there first.

reading-flood-news/millimetres-decoded.text: Each millimetre of rain means one litre of water on a square metre.

reading-flood-news/radar-decoded.text: Radar maps show where rain was falling a short time ago. The key explains the colours.

reading-flood-news/three-questions.text: Good listeners ask three questions. How much rain? Where is the water going? Is the level rising?

river-reservoir-sea/basin.text: Rain in the hills runs into streams. The streams join and become a river. The land that sends water to it is the river basin.

river-reservoir-sea/bottleneck.text: When a narrow stretch cannot carry all the water arriving, the water level rises upstream. This is called backwater.

river-reservoir-sea/closing.text: River water travels downhill towards another river, a lake or the sea.

river-reservoir-sea/in-and-out.text: Water flowing into the reservoir is inflow. The dam releases water for the river, the farms and the towns below.

river-reservoir-sea/level-rises.text: When more water comes, the river rises. People watch its water level.

river-reservoir-sea/one-system.text: Rain, streams, reservoirs, rivers and the sea are one system. Water moves through all of it, every day.

river-reservoir-sea/reservoir.text: A dam is a strong wall across a valley. The lake behind it is the reservoir.

river-reservoir-sea/tide-gate.text: The river mouth is where the river ends at the sea. At high tide the sea level is higher, and the river flows out more slowly.

river-reservoir-sea/upstream-travels.text: Rain that falls upstream in the hills travels downstream. It reaches different places at different times.

space-trip/back-home.text: The stars keep shining. Goodnight, planets!

space-trip/earth-moon.text: Earth is our home planet. The Moon travels around Earth.

space-trip/jupiter.text: Jupiter is the biggest planet. Its clouds form colorful bands and giant storms.

space-trip/saturn.text: Saturn has beautiful rings. Its rings are made of pieces of ice and rock.

space-trip/solar-system.text: Our solar system has the Sun and eight planets. It also has moons, asteroids, and comets.

space-trip/sun.text: The Sun is a star. It gives Earth light and heat.

stars-life-cycle/a-sun-like-stars-future.text: A star like the Sun swells into a red giant. Later, its hot core remains as a small white dwarf.

stars-life-cycle/a-supernova.text: A very big star can end in a huge explosion called a supernova. It sends star material out into space.

stars-life-cycle/big-stars-live-fast.text: Very big stars use their fuel quickly. Their lives are much shorter than the Sun's life.

stars-life-cycle/born-in-a-nebula.text: Stars are born inside huge clouds of gas and dust called nebulae. Gravity pulls the material together.

stars-life-cycle/cover.text: How Stars Are Born and Change

stars-life-cycle/goodnight-changing-star.text: Stars are born, shine and change across an enormous stretch of time. Goodnight, stars of the past and stars still to come.

stars-life-cycle/light-from-the-core.text: Deep in a star's core, enormous pressure squeezes tiny bits together. This is fusion, and it makes light and heat.

stars-life-cycle/made-of-star-stuff.text: Material from old stars helps make new stars and planets. The elements in our bodies were made by stars.

stars-life-cycle/our-middle-aged-sun.text: Our Sun is a medium-sized star. It is about halfway through its long life.

stars/closest-star.text: The Sun is a star. It is the closest star to Earth.

stars/far-away.text: Other stars are very far away. That is why they look like tiny points of light.

stars/find-orion.text: People join stars into patterns called constellations. The children find Orion and his three bright belt stars.

stars/goodnight-stars.text: The stars shine on as the children grow sleepy. Goodnight, stars!

stars/star-colours.text: Stars have different colours. Blue stars are hotter, and red stars are cooler.

stars/stars-at-night.text: As night falls, stars shine above the hill. The children look up together.

stars/why-stars-twinkle.text: Starlight bends as it passes through Earth's moving air. That makes the stars seem to twinkle.

stay-out-of-floodwater/animals-need-dry-.text: Floods can make animals leave their usual homes. We do not touch them. We tell a grown-up.

stay-out-of-floodwater/bottom-is-hidden.text: Floodwater hides the bottom. You cannot always see where your next step will land.

stay-out-of-floodwater/cover.text: Why We Stay Out of Floodwater

stay-out-of-floodwater/hidden-objects.text: Floodwater can hide branches, metal, rubbish and broken things that can hurt us.

stay-out-of-floodwater/not-clean-play-wa.text: Water from roads, drains, rubbish and muddy soil can mix together. Floodwater can carry dirty water and germs.

stay-out-of-floodwater/pool-or-floodwate.text: A swimming pool and a flooded road both have water. Are they the same? No. Floodwater can have dangers we cannot see.

stay-out-of-floodwater/stronger-than-it-.text: Moving water can be much stronger than it looks. Even people who can swim should stay out of floodwater.

stay-out-of-floodwater/water-and-electri.text: If water reaches damaged electrical things, stay away and tell a grown-up.

stay-out-of-floodwater/what-should-i-do.text: Water where it should not be? Stay out. Something fell in? Tell a grown-up. Electrical thing near water? Stay away. Need to go somewhere? Stay with your grown-up. Floodwater does not have to look scary to be dangerous.

street-under-water/hard-to-see.text: Some dangers are hidden. Some are too small to see.

street-under-water/look-under-water.text: The water did not make the street smooth. It only hid the street.

street-under-water/our-street.text: This is our street. We know where to walk: along the pavement, beside the curb.

street-under-water/rain-keeps-falling.text: Now water covers the street. It looks different.

street-under-water/same-place-different-.text: Same place. Different rules. When water covers places that are normally dry, stay with a grown-up and stay out of the floodwater.

street-under-water/water-can-move.text: Floodwater can push things. Water that looks calm can still be moving.

street-under-water/water-connects-places.text: Floodwater connects the road, drain, garden, rubbish area and canal. It can bring things from somewhere else.

street-under-water/where-did-everything-.text: Can you still see the curb? Can you see the drain? Can you see the hole? They are still there. The water is hiding them.

when-water-goes-away/adults-check-and-cl.text: Grown-ups check electrical things, clear debris, clean and dry belongings, and open safe paths. They make our neighbourhood safe again.

when-water-goes-away/animals-may-be-hidi.text: Animals may have moved while looking for dry places. Let a grown-up check.

when-water-goes-away/check-before-using.text: Things touched by floodwater may need to be cleaned or thrown away. A grown-up checks before we touch or eat them.

when-water-goes-away/left-behind.text: Floodwater can leave mud, leaves, rubbish and dirty things behind.

when-water-goes-away/safe-again.text: The flood changed our neighbourhood for a while. We stayed safe, people worked together, and now we can use our familiar places again.

when-water-goes-away/sharp-things.text: Broken things can hide in mud and rubbish. Adults check before children come back.

when-water-goes-away/water-going-down.text: The water is going away! But we still need to be careful.

when-water-goes-away/wet-electrical-thin.text: Wet electrical things need to be checked by grown-ups.

where-rain-goes/canals-to-river.text: Drains lead to canals. Canals lead to rivers. Rivers carry water to the sea.

where-rain-goes/closing.text: Our paper boats follow the water downhill. Next time it rains, watch where the water goes!

where-rain-goes/drains.text: In towns, water slips into drains under the street.

where-rain-goes/full-sponge.text: A sponge can fill up. Soil that is full of water is called saturated soil. When rain comes faster than full soil can take it in, water stays on top.

where-rain-goes/one-journey-map.text: Every drop of rain takes one of these journeys. Water that is stored can journey again another day.

where-rain-goes/rain-lands.text: Rain lands on soil, grass, roofs and roads. Each landing is the start of a different journey.

where-rain-goes/runoff.text: Extra water flows across the ground. This flowing water is called runoff. It slides to lower places.

where-rain-goes/soil-sponge.text: Soil is like a sponge. It drinks the rain.

where-rain-goes/storage.text: People also catch rain. Tanks, ponds and reservoirs keep it for dry days.

where-rain-goes/sun-takes-water.text: Some water waits in puddles and leaves. The sun lifts it back up as vapour. This is evaporation.

why-places-flood/closing.text: Next time a puddle grows, we can ask: where can this water go?

why-places-flood/drain-full.text: A drain can only carry so much water. This limit is its drainage capacity. Extra rain waits on the street.

why-places-flood/ground-full.text: Ground that is already wet takes in new rain slowly. Rain that comes faster stays on top.

why-places-flood/low-places.text: A low-lying area is low ground. Water slides there and fills it first.

why-places-flood/neighbors-differ.text: Two houses on one street can have different elevations. The lower one sits in water first.

why-places-flood/river-high.text: When the water level in the river is higher than the canal, its gate closes. Pumps push the water out instead.

why-places-flood/the-rule.text: A place floods when water comes in faster than it can flow away.

why-places-flood/watching-the-level.text: People read a staff gauge to watch the water level. Rising or falling is the big question.

why-places-flood/water-waits.text: Flood water is patient. It recedes when the drains and rivers have room again.

what-computers-do/closing.text: Can you find a computer with a screen and one without a screen?

what-computers-do/computers-inside.text: A washing machine has a small computer inside. A traffic-light system uses a controller in a roadside cabinet.

what-computers-do/exactly.text: A computer follows the exact instructions in its program. If the instructions are wrong, the output can be wrong too.

what-computers-do/input.text: A tap, typed word, picture, or sound can be input. Input is information a computer receives.

what-computers-do/instructions-inside.text: People create programs with instructions. Computers follow these instructions to do different jobs.

what-computers-do/many-jobs.text: A computer can show pictures, play songs, and help you write.

what-computers-do/output.text: Output is information a computer produces. It can be a picture, sound, words, or movement.

what-computers-do/three-steps.text: A computer takes in information, follows instructions, and produces a result.

what-computers-do/very-fast.text: Computers can carry out many instructions very fast. Speed helps them do big jobs one small step at a time.
